 Judgment
Dated this the 10th day of April, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No. 757/2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ottapalam, is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 01.02.2010.

According to the petitioner, on 01.02.2010 at about 9.00 p.m., while he was traveling in a bus bearing Reg.No. KL 9V 7177 driven by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner through Kozhikode-Palakkad public road, it hit against a lorry bearing Reg.No. TN 45 E 7295 driven by the 4 th respondent and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the bus.
Respondents 4 to 6 are the driver, owner and insurer of the lorry.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the bus.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.6,76,500(limited to 6,00,000/-).
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A13, X1 and B1.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the bus, awarded a total compensation of Rs. 7,02,200/- and directed the insurer/3rd respondent to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:

sentences.text: Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri.Jacob Sebastian, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.
Mathews Jacob, the learned Senior Standing Counsel as instructed by Sri, P. Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by 2025:KER:33031 the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as Goldsmith by profession, earning Rs. 500/- per day, but the Tribunal has fixed his monthly income at Rs.3500/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2010 will come to Rs.7,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner being a goldsmith by profession, his notional income is fixed at Rs.9000/-, for the purpose of computing the loss of disability.
12. In the accident the petitioner sustained segmental amputation Rt.upper limb and traumatic amputation right arm above elbow.
13. As per Exhibit X1, the disability certificate, the petitioner suffered 60% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by the medical board.
As per the Employees Compensation Act, Schedule-I Part II, Item No. 2, amputation below shoulder with stump less than 20.32 cms. from tip of acromion amounts to 80% loss of earning capacity.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, since the petitioner was a goldsmith by profession, 2025:KER:33031 his functional disability is to be taken as 100%.

He has also relied upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rekha Jain v. National Insurance Co. Ltd [2012 KHC 4600], in which the victim was a film and TV artist whose face was disfigured in the accident.

entities.text: Rekha Jain v. National Insurance Co. Ltd [2012 KHC 4600]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though her physical disability was 30%, the Apex court fixed her functional disability at 100%.
In the instant case, the petitioner lost his right hand above the elbow and below the shoulder and as such, he could not continue his profession as a goldsmith.

Therefore, his functional disability is taken as 100%.
14.
On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 24 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

entities.text:
National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.27,21,600/-
15.
Since the functional disability of the petitioner was taken as 100%, he is not entitled to get compensation on the head loss of earnings.
Therefore, the loss of earnings awarded by the Tribunal will be deducted.

sentences.text:
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has 2025:KER:33031 awarded Rs.25,000/-
and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.1400/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.

The Tribunal has not awarded any amount on the head 'loss of amenities'.
17.
The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 7 days.
He lost his right hand in the accident.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', extra nourishment' and 'loss of amenities of life' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-,
10,000/- and 2,00,000/- respectively.
18.

The petitioner has produced Annexure A4 invoice and claims that towards the cost of prosthesis,
he needs a sum of Rs.16,94,175/-.
However, the learned counsel for the insurer would argue that it is only a voucher and not a receipt and as such, the same cannot be considered.

However, the fact remains that the right hand of the petitioner below the shoulder was amputated and as such, he requires a prosthesis for the rest of his life.
19.

In the decision in Vivek. G. v. National Insurance Co. Ltd 2025:KER:33031 [2023 KHC 2941], in the case of a 12 year old child whose right leg was amputated in the year 2011, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has awarded a sum of Rs. 26,000,00/- towards the cost of four prosthesis and the cost of maintenance.

entities.text: Vivek. G. v. National Insurance Co. Ltd 2025:KER:33031 [2023 KHC 2941]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in that case, the cost of one prosthesis for the right leg was taken by the apex court at Rs. 5,00,000/-.

In the instant case, the prosthesis is required for the hand and as such, in the absence of reliable evidence, I hold that a consolidated sum of Rs. 10,00,000/- can be awarded towards the cost of the prosthesis and its maintenance.
20. Towards marriage prospects, the Tribunal has not awarded any amount.
I hold that the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs. 2,00,000/- towards loss of marriage prospects.

Therefore,
Rs.200000/- awarded on the head 'Compensation for continuing partial or permanent disability'
will be adjusted towards 'loss of marriage prospects'.
21.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
22. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.32,61,500/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

 power/disability  9 Compensation for continuing Rs.2,00,000/- 200000/- (treated   partial or permanent disability of marriage prospe  10 Loss of amenities NIL Rs.2,00,000/-

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.32,61,500/-, (Rupees Thirty two lakhs sixty one thousand and five hundred only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, excluding interest for a period of 673 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).
24.

On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse 2025:KER:33031 25% of the entire amount, excluding court fee payable, if any, to the petitioner,
forthwith.

25. The Tribunal is permitted to decide, after considering the welfare, well being and the best interest of the petitioner, whether the balance amount is to be disbursed in full, forthwith or in installments or to be deposited in a Nationalised bank in fixed deposit in the name of the petitioner and to permit withdrawal of interest alone for the time being.

26. The Tribunal found that, at the time of the accident, there was no valid driving licence for the 1st respondent and as such the insurer was permitted to recover the compensation from respondents 1 and 2.

Before this court also the respondents 1 and 2 have not produced the valid driving licence of the 1st respondent and as such I do not find any grounds to interfere with the above finding of the Tribunal.

Therefore,
the permission granted for recovery from respondents 1 and 2 is retained.
